_comment: Scope rules this project asserts about itself. They live here, not in a local note,
because a note is gone after a machine change and gets re-decided by the next pass
over the tree. `scope_gate.py` checks all three rules on every push.
S1 identity_sweep_exceptions: a literal that an external system hardcodes. The identity
sweep (grep for the upstream project name) must leave it alone: renaming it points
that external system at a path which does not exist, and nothing local notices.
S2 out_of_scope: a switch this plan does not own; it must keep the listed value.
S3 every entry carries `why` and `exit`, so an exception cannot be added without
saying what it is for and what would remove it.
The two incidents behind S1/S2 are recorded in workspace/audit/gaps.md as G-42 and G-43.

identity_sweep_exceptions.why: The ops server deploys benchmark bundles into /tmp/fcpp_benchmark_* and those directories are created outside this repository. The name is the deploy target, not the project identity; renaming it to the project prefix sends the deploy tool to a directory that does not exist, and every local gate still passes.
identity_sweep_exceptions.exit: never: the literal belongs to the deploy host. If the ops side renames the directories, update `must_contain` in the same change.

out_of_scope.why: benchmark/platform/*.json lists the physical devices wired into CI (hardware in the loop, the self-hosted board route). This plan covers the virtualised matrix under .github/project/qa only, so the board route stays off and no :fire: commit is pushed.
out_of_scope.exit: turn it on in the plan that owns hardware, not here.
